sources.entry: OATS - Open-source local-first meeting-notes app for macOS with live transcription, speaker labels, AI summaries, and a fully offline on-device mode. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/ariso-ai/oats) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]
OATS - Open-source local-first macOS meeting-notes app with live transcription, speaker labels, AI summaries, and an offline on-device mode.

summary.one_liner: oats is an open-source meeting-notes app for macOS (and Windows) that records meetings from the menu bar, transcribes them live, labels speakers, and writes Markdown notes, either through a free cloud backend or fully offline on-device.
summary.what_it_does: The app sits in the menu bar with one-click record, pause, resume, and stop. It streams a real-time transcription while people talk and tags speakers. Each recording gets an automatic Markdown summary and is kept in a library alongside its transcript. Sharing uses the native macOS share sheet or the Ariso web backend. In Local mode, recording, transcription, speaker labels, and notes all run on the machine, with models downloaded once through Settings. Files are saved under ~/.ariso/recordings/ as recording.mp3, transcript.md, and ari-note.md.
use_cases: record and transcribe meetings on a Mac
generate meeting summaries and notes automatically
private on-device meeting notes without uploading audio
menu bar voice recorder for calls
how_to_run: Alternatively, download oats.dmg from the Releases page, drag oats into Applications, and launch it.
On first launch, choose a transcription backend in Settings → Transcription Backend (Ariso cloud or Local).
For Local mode, open Settings → On-device models and install the speech model and language model.
notable: Local mode runs recording, transcription, speaker labels, and notes fully offline with no login or upload
Cloud mode (Ariso) is free and needs no setup beyond signing in
Transcription on macOS uses CoreML on the Apple Neural Engine
Signed, notarized, and auto-updating macOS build installed via Homebrew cask or DMG
caveats: Full support is for macOS 14+ on Apple Silicon; Windows 11 is in release preview and Windows 10 is not public-support ready
Cloud mode stores transcripts on the Ariso backend and requires an account; multi-language is only available in cloud mode
Homebrew 6.0+ requires a one-time brew trust step for the third-party tap
